paye band 2 rate: PAYE second band rate is 8% on income between TZS 270,001 and TZS 520,000
paye penalty rate: Late PAYE remittance penalty is 2.5% per month of unpaid amount

paye personal relief: Tanzania has NO separate PAYE personal relief deduction. The 0% band on first TZS 270,000/month IS the effective tax-free amount. Both TZS 26,000 and TZS 27,000 'personal relief' figures are WRONG.
paye p9 deadline: Annual PAYE reconciliation Form P9 deadline is 31 March of following year — NOT 31 January
p45 not tanzanian: Form P45 does not exist in Tanzania — it is a UK payroll form. Use P9 or leaving certificate.
SDL (Skills Development Levy) Tanzania: asilimia 3.5 ya mishahara yote. Si 4%, si 2%.
sdl full name: SDL stands for Skills Development Levy — NOT Service Delivery Levy and NOT short-term disability leave
Kizingiti cha SDL ni wafanyakazi 10 au zaidi. Wafanyakazi 10 hasa wanalipa SDL (wako ndani). Si 11, si 4.
sdl payer: SDL is paid by the employer only — NOT deducted from employee wages
NSSF: mwajiri analipa asilimia 10 ya mshahara wa mfanyakazi kila mwezi. Tovuti sahihi ni nssf.go.tz (si nssf.or.tz).
NSSF jumla: asilimia 20 ya mshahara (10% mwajiri + 10% mfanyakazi). Tovuti sahihi ni nssf.go.tz (si nssf.or.tz).
nssf penalty: NSSF late payment penalty is 5% per month of unpaid contributions
nssf retirement age: NSSF retirement age is 60 (55 for mining/early retirement), minimum 180 months contributions for full pension
vat standard rate: Tanzania VAT standard rate is 18% — unchanged since 2015. It was NEVER 14%.
vat reduced rates: Tanzania does NOT have reduced VAT rates of 5% or 10%. Only 18% standard, 0% zero-rated, and exempt.
vat registration threshold: VAT registration threshold is TZS 200,000,000 per year OR TZS 100,000,000 per 6 months
vat withholding goods: VAT withholding on goods is 3% — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025)
vat withholding services: VAT withholding on services is 6% — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025)
gn487a nature: GN487A is a BUSINESS PROHIBITION ORDER listing 15 activities non-citizens cannot conduct. It is NOT about immigration or residence permits.
gn487a effective date: GN 487A came into effect on 28 July 2025
Faini kwa mgeni (raia wa kigeni) anayevunja GN487A: si chini ya TZS 10,000,000 (milioni kumi), na/au kifungo miezi 6, na kufutwa kwa visa.
Adhabu kwa raia wa Tanzania anayemsaidia mgeni kukiuka GN487A: faini si zaidi ya TZS 5,000,000 (milioni tano), au kifungo si zaidi ya miezi 3.
gn605a effective date: GN 605A Private Sector Wage Order came into effect on 1 January 2026
gn605a average increase: GN 605A average increase is 33.4% from TZS 275,060 to TZS 358,322 per month
royalties wht rate: Withholding tax on royalties is 15% for BOTH residents and non-residents
provisional tax instalments: Provisional tax is paid in FOUR equal instalments at end of months 3, 6, 9, and 12 from start of financial year
minimum turnover tax: Tanzania minimum turnover tax is 1% of gross turnover effective 1 July 2025 — was 0.5%, never 0.3%
commissioner objection deadline: TRA Commissioner must determine an objection within 6 months from date of admission — NOT 90 days
trab appeal two steps: TRAB appeal requires TWO steps: (1) Notice of Intention within 30 days AND (2) Statement of Appeal within 45 days
objection deposit requirement: Before TRA objection is admitted taxpayer must pay the HIGHER of undisputed tax OR one-third of assessed tax within 15 days
objection extension statutory right: Extension of the 30-day objection period is a STATUTORY RIGHT — NOT very rare. Apply within 7 days before expiry.
stamp duty property transfer: Stamp duty on transfer of land or buildings is a FLAT 1% of consideration or market value — NOT tiered 0.5%/1%
permit class b employed: Class B Residence Permit is for EMPLOYED EXPATRIATES working for companies — NOT for investors
permit class a investor: Class A Residence Permit is for SELF-EMPLOYED FOREIGN INVESTORS — NOT Class B
permit class c categories: Class C Residence Permit is for researchers, retired persons, missionaries, volunteers — NOT for employed foreign workers
corporate tax rate: Tanzania standard corporate income tax rate is 30%. DSE-listed companies pay 25%.
wht deadline: Withholding tax must be remitted within 7 DAYS after end of the calendar month — NOT 7th of following month
loss carryforward finance act 2024: After 4 consecutive years of tax losses only 60% of year 5 income can be offset against losses (Finance Act 2024)
brela share transfer legal effect: Share transfer without BRELA notification MAY LACK LEGAL EFFECT AGAINST THIRD PARTIES — it is not absolutely void
tmda replaces tfda: TMDA (Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority) is the current name — TFDA no longer exists

brave search blocked tanzania: Brave Search API is blocked in Tanzania. TRA required Brave Software to register as non-resident electronic service provider. Brave blocked Tanzania access instead of registering.
paye all bands sequence: PAYE bands (monthly): 0% up to TZS 270K | 8% TZS 270K-520K | 20% TZS 520K-760K | 25% TZS 760K-1M | 30% above TZS 1M
paye nonresident flat rate: Non-resident employees pay PAYE at a flat 15% rate — NOT the progressive bands. This is a final withholding tax.
brela annual return fee: BRELA annual return filing fee is TZS 22,000. Late filing penalty is TZS 2,500 per month (local company) or USD 25/month (foreign Section XII company).
wcf new employer registration: A new employer must register with WCF within 30 days of hiring their first employee

wcf disease reporting deadline: Occupational disease must be reported to WCF within 7 working days of diagnosis. Workplace death must be reported within 12 months. Compensation claim must be filed within 12 months of accident or disease discovery.
gn605a increment range: GN 605A individual sector increments range from TZS 20,000 (lowest sector) to TZS 195,000 (highest sector) per month
unresolved items:
wht director fees: WHT on director fees (non-full-time directors) is 15% — a single rate for both residents and non-residents. Source: TRA.go.tz withholding tax page.

wcf accident reporting: Employer must notify WCF of a workplace accident within 7 WORKING DAYS — via WCF online portal (portal.wcf.go.tz). Different deadline for occupational illness. Source: WCF portal.
wcf accident reporting deadline: 7 working days from date of accident. Source: Workers Compensation Act / portal.wcf.go.tz
OSHA Tanzania: kila mwajiri lazima asajili mahali pa kazi na OSHA. Sheria inahusu maeneo yote ya kazi bila kikomo cha idadi ya wafanyakazi.
dse 25 rate three years only: DSE 25% CIT rate applies for THREE YEARS ONLY from listing date
amt loss companies only: AMT 1% applies ONLY to companies with 3 consecutive years of tax losses
permit class d does not exist: Tanzania has NO Class D permit — only Class A (investor), Class B (employed expatriate), Class C (researcher/voluntary)
gn487a transitional provision: Non-citizens with valid licences at 28 July 2025 may continue until licence expiry. No renewal permitted. No new licences issued for prohibited activities.

efd threshold tzs 11m: EFD required for businesses with annual turnover TZS 11 million and above. Below TZS 11M may use manual receipts. All VAT-registered businesses must use EFD regardless of turnover.

gn487a visa revocation: Visa revocation is a possible consequence — not universally mandatory in all sources. Bowmans says AND/mandatory. The Star and The Citizen say possible/risk. Train model to say CAN be revoked not WILL always be revoked.
vat withholding remittance deadline: VAT withholding remitted to TRA by 20th of following month — same deadline as VAT return. NOT 7 days after month end.
vat late registration penalty: Penalty for failure to register VAT: fine up to TZS 200,000 AND/OR imprisonment 2-12 months PLUS interest on unpaid VAT. NO 2.5% monthly rate exists in the VAT Act.
NSSF inalipwa ifikapo tarehe 10 ya mwezi unaofuata.
sdl rate 2025: SDL rate is 3.5% of gross cash emoluments effective 1 July 2023 (Finance Act 2023 reduced from 4%). Minimum 10 employees threshold applies.
Kizingiti cha SDL: mwajiri mwenye wafanyakazi 10 AU ZAIDI analipa SDL. Mwenye wafanyakazi 10 YUKO NDANI ya kizingiti na analipa SDL. Chini ya 10 (yaani 9 au pungufu) hawalipi SDL.

paye bands monthly 2025 26: PAYE monthly bands 2025/26: Band 1: 0-270,000=0%; Band 2: 270,001-520,000=8%; Band 3: 520,001-760,000=20%; Band 4: 760,001-1,000,000=25%; Band 5: above 1,000,000=30%. No personal relief of TZS 26,000 exists.

vat withholding formula correct: VAT withholding rate applies to the VAT AMOUNT, not the invoice/contract value. Goods: 3% x VAT amount. Services: 6% x VAT amount. Example goods: TZS 1M invoice, VAT = TZS 180,000, withholding = TZS 5,400 (3% x 180,000). Supplier receives TZS 1,174,600 (invoice + VAT minus withheld). Example services: TZS 1M invoice, VAT = TZS 180,000, withholding = TZS 10,800 (6% x 180,000). Supplier receives TZS 1,169,200.

wcf threshold no minimum: WCF (Workers Compensation Fund) applies to ALL employers in Mainland Tanzania from the first employee. There is NO minimum employee count threshold. Contrast with SDL which requires 10+ employees. WCF: 0.5% of gross cash emoluments, from employee 1. SDL: 3.5% of gross cash emoluments, from employee 10.
WCF (Workers Compensation Fund): mwajiri analipa asilimia 0.5 ya jumla ya mishahara yote kila mwezi. Si kiasi kisichobadilika — inategemea mishahara.

vat threshold 200m july2024 increase: VAT registration threshold was increased from TZS 100M to TZS 200M in July 2024. Current thresholds: TZS 200M per 12 months OR TZS 100M per any 6-month rolling period. Zanzibar threshold is separate (TZS 100M) — different jurisdiction. Any pair showing TZS 100M/year or TZS 50M/6mo is citing pre-July-2024 rules.

GN605A effective date: GN 605A (Government Notice No. 605A) gazetted 13 October 2025, effective 1 January 2026. Revokes and replaces the Minimum Wage Order 2022 in its entirety. The 2022 order has NO force after 31 December 2025.

GN605A sector count: GN 605A establishes minimum wages across 16 main sectors with multiple subsectors. There is no single flat national rate — each sector and subsector has its own distinct monthly minimum. Training pairs must not state a single flat rate as applying to all workers.

GN605A rate range: GN 605A monthly rates range from TZS 80,000 (other domestic workers) to TZS 765,900 (energy sector international companies). Agricultural/general floor is TZS 175,000. Any sector not explicitly specified in the Order defaults to TZS 175,000 per month.

GN605A key sector rates: Selected confirmed GN 605A monthly minimum rates: Agricultural (crop/animal): TZS 175,000. Hotel 5-star/4-star: TZS 375,000. Hotel bars/restaurants: TZS 195,000. Mining (prospecting): TZS 695,000. Energy international: TZS 765,900. Commercial banks: TZS 733,000. Construction Class I: TZS 515,000. Telecommunication: TZS 644,000. Industrial: TZS 200,000.

OSHA penalties: Failure to register or obtain OSHA compliance licence: fine TZS 1,000,000 to TZS 5,000,000 OR imprisonment up to 12 months OR both. Continuing offence: additional TZS 100,000 per day. Source: OHS Act No. 5 of 2003.

VAT withholding base disputed: The base for VAT withholding calculation is DISPUTED between sources. TRA.go.tz says 3% of the consideration (invoice total) for goods, 6% of consideration for services. PwC Tax Summaries says 3% of VAT amount for goods, 6% of VAT amount for services. These produce very different results. Training pairs must NOT state a specific calculation formula — use 'thibitisha na TRA kwa hesabu sahihi' instead.

NSSF split triggers: NSSF total is always 20% of gross wage. Three valid employer-employee split arrangements: (a) 10% employer + 10% employee — standard default; (b) 15% employer + 5% employee — employer elects to contribute more; (c) 20% employer + 0% employee — employer pays the full 20%, employee pays nothing. Employee share must never exceed 10%. All three arrangements are legal under the NSSF Act.

BRELA fees hedge: BRELA registration and filing fees change periodically via ministerial order. Training pairs must direct users to brela.go.tz or the ORS portal for current fees rather than stating specific TZS amounts. The annual return filing fee has been approximately TZS 22,000 but this must be verified before quoting in any business context.

vat withholding certificate timing: VAT withholding certificate must be issued NOT LATER THAN the date on which VAT becomes payable under section 15 of the VAT Act — NOT on the 20th of the following month. The 20th deadline applies to filing the VAT return and remitting the withheld amount, which are separate obligations. A withholding agent must issue the certificate in an approved system format containing: TIN, registration number, supply description, consideration amount, withholding rate and withholding amount.

brela partnership registration: A general partnership (ushirikiano wa kibiashara) in Tanzania can be registered with BRELA under the Business Names Registration Act or incorporated as a Limited Partnership. Required documents typically include: partnership deed, names and addresses of all partners, business name, nature of business, TIN for each partner. Exact current procedure and fees must be verified at brela.go.tz or via the ORS portal (ors.brela.go.tz) as requirements change by ministerial order.

osha licence renewal frequency: OSHA workplace compliance certificate (cheti cha usajilishaji) renewal frequency is not explicitly stated on osha.go.tz. The OHS Act 2003 requires employers to maintain workplace registration. In practice OSHA conducts annual risk assessments and inspections. Training pairs must direct employers to osha.go.tz to confirm current renewal period rather than stating a specific interval.

nssf employer registration deadline: Every employer in Tanzania must register with NSSF before or within a reasonable period of commencing business. The NSSF Act Cap. 50 imposes a registration obligation but the exact number of days is not confirmed from the primary source (nssf.go.tz was unreachable during verification). Training pairs must direct employers to nssf.go.tz to confirm current registration deadline and avoid stating a specific day count.

efd approved supplier verification: To verify that an EFD supplier/distributor (msambazaji) is TRA-approved, businesses should check the official TRA website (tra.go.tz) for the current list of approved EFD dealers. TRA publishes a register of approved EFD suppliers. Businesses should only purchase EFD machines from TRA-approved dealers — purchasing from unapproved suppliers may result in the machine not being activated by TRA. The TRA EFD page URL changed and was unavailable at time of writing.
OSHA hufanya ukaguzi wa lazima kila mwaka (mara moja kwa mwaka) katika maeneo yote ya kazi Tanzania.

OSHA safety officer threshold: The specific employee threshold requiring a dedicated safety officer is NOT confirmed from authoritative sources. Training pairs must NOT state a specific number (e.g. 50 employees). Direct users to osha.go.tz for current requirements.

BRELA COSOTA split: Intellectual property in Tanzania is split between two bodies. BRELA (Business Registrations and Licensing Agency) administers: trademarks (alama za biashara), patents (hati miliki), and industrial designs (miundo ya viwanda). COSOTA (Copyright Society of Tanzania) administers: copyright and neighbouring rights (haki za ubunifu na haki jirani). There is NO body called ORT — ort.go.tz does not exist as a Tanzanian IP registry.

SDL source law: SDL (Skills Development Levy) is imposed under Section 14 of the Vocational Education Training Act, Cap. 82. It is collected by TRA. Rate: 3.5% of gross cash emoluments (reduced from 4% by Finance Act 2023, effective 1 July 2023). Applies to employers with 10 or more employees on Mainland Tanzania.

VAT zero rated vs exempt input VAT: Zero-rated supplies are taxable at 0% VAT rate — suppliers CAN claim input VAT on their purchases. Exempt supplies are not subject to VAT at all — suppliers CANNOT claim input VAT on their purchases. These are fundamentally different categories. The model previously inverted this rule (eval_017 failure: stated zero-rated businesses cannot claim input VAT).

gn487a mgeni cap357 definition: GN487A defines 'non-citizen' by reference to the Tanzania Citizenship Act Cap.357 R.E.2023. Cap.357 recognises three citizen categories: citizen by birth, citizen by descent, and citizen by naturalisation. A person holding Tanzanian citizenship under any of these three categories is NOT a non-citizen for GN487A purposes. Whether dual nationals holding a Tanzanian passport qualify as citizens depends on Cap.357 — this is a legal interpretation that must be verified with an immigration lawyer.

gn487a msaidizi definition: Under GN487A, a 'msaidizi' (facilitator) is a Tanzanian citizen who assists or aids a non-citizen to carry out any of the 15 prohibited business activities. This includes but may not be limited to lending their name, business licence, or identity to allow a non-citizen to operate a prohibited business. Penalty for msaidizi: TZS 5,000,000 fine OR imprisonment not exceeding 3 months. The facilitator and the non-citizen are BOTH penalised.

gn487a marriage no exemption: Marriage to a Tanzanian citizen does NOT grant GN487A exemption. Citizenship under Tanzania Citizenship Act Cap.357 requires formal naturalisation — marriage alone does not confer citizenship. A foreign national married to a Tanzanian remains a non-citizen for GN487A purposes and is still prohibited from conducting the 15 listed business activities. The path to GN487A exemption is acquiring Tanzanian citizenship through formal naturalisation, not marriage.

vat withholding buyer remits directly: The withholding agent (qualifying buyer / mnunuzi anayehitimu) remits VAT withholding DIRECTLY to TRA — not through the supplier's VAT return. TRA states: 'the withholding agent shall withhold 3%/6% and remit it to the Commissioner General.' The supplier receives a VAT Withholding Certificate as proof that the withheld amount has been remitted. The formula base (consideration vs VAT amount) remains disputed — see VAT_withholding_base_disputed.

efd tra closure authority: TRA has enforcement authority against businesses that repeatedly fail to issue EFD receipts. Enforcement actions can include: written warnings, imposition of fines, suspension of EFD device/licence, and closure of business premises. The TRA EFD page was unavailable at time of verification (June 2026) but closure authority is grounded in the VAT Act Cap.148 enforcement provisions and general TRA administrative powers under the Tax Administration Act.

gn487a full legal name: GN 487A is Government Notice No. 487A. Its full legal name is: The Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order, 2025. GN 487A is NOT Government Notice No. 605A. Government Notice No. 605A is a completely different instrument -- the 2026 minimum wage order. Never state that GN 487A's name or number is 605A.

gn487a vs gn605a disambiguation: GN 487A and GN 605A are two DIFFERENT Government Notices and must never be conflated. GN 487A = Government Notice No. 487A = The Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order, 2025 (effective 28 July 2025; bars non-citizens from 15 business activities). GN 605A = Government Notice No. 605A = the Private Sector Minimum Wage Order (gazetted 13 October 2025, effective 1 January 2026; sets minimum wages, revokes the 2022 wage order). Different numbers, different subjects, different Ministries. Asking for GN 487A's name must NOT return 605A, and asking about minimum wage must NOT return 487A.

gn487a shareholder vs operator distinction: GN487A prohibits non-citizens from CONDUCTING or OPERATING the listed business activities. Passive shareholding or investment in a Tanzanian-owned and operated company is not explicitly prohibited by GN487A - the prohibition targets the person carrying out the activity, not the investor. However, a non-citizen who is a shareholder AND actively manages or operates the business would be covered. Consult an immigration lawyer for specific structures.
